facility_roles.quote: This document is focused on a project of the Super Charm Tau factory in the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics (Novosibirsk, Russia).

intervals.label: Super Charm-Tau factory project at BINP
intervals.locator: SCTF Conceptual Design Report, Part One, title page
intervals.note: Start = the 2018 conceptual design report (a 'very preliminary draft'); earlier tau-charm factory studies at BINP are cited in it (SLAC-Report-451, 1994; a 1995 'C-Tau in Novosibirsk' CDR) but are a different design. In 2020 BINP was still 'developing a Super Charm-Tau factory project' (arXiv:2005.09878). No approval, funding or construction is reported in the sources fetched, and none is dated after 2020; the project status as of 2026-10-26 is not confirmed.
intervals.quote: CONCEPTUAL DESIGN REPORT PART ONE (physics program, detector) [very preliminary draft] Novosibirsk 2018

name: SCTF
notes: No collaboration record exists: the CDR author list (about 150 names at BINP, Novosibirsk State University, Sobolev Institute, Boreskov Institute of Catalysis and others) is a project team, and no named collaboration was found.

The BINP project page and CDR describe the project as the BINP response to the high-luminosity B factories and to the crab-waist collision scheme; no successor relation to an existing Atlas experiment is stated.

physics_goals.quote: The main purpose of the experiments at the collider is search for effects of CP-violation in the decays of charmed particles, tests of the Standard Model in the decay of the tau lepton, the search and study of an entirely new form of matter: glueballs, hybrids, etc.
physics_goals.value: Charm and tau physics: CP violation in charmed-particle decays, tests of the Standard Model in tau decays, and a search for glueballs and hybrids

summary.plain: The experiment planned for the proposed Super Charm-Tau Factory at the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk: a universal magnetic detector to record the huge samples of charm particles and tau leptons from 2 to 5 GeV collisions. Only a 2018 preliminary design exists.
summary.technical: SCTF: universal magnetic detector with high momentum resolution for charged particles, very high photon energy resolution, record particle identification (FARICH aerogel Cherenkov) and a data-acquisition system for 300-400 kHz event rates; CDR Part One (physics and detector), very preliminary draft, BINP 2018. Status after 2020 not found.
